about: One row per Cast model name (the md of its DNS-SD record, compared without case): every video codec Google's 'Supported Media for Google Cast' (developers.google.com/cast/docs/media, read 2026-11-25; the page gives no date) lists for it, with its profile, level and the modes it allows, in the order the daemon prefers them (the first one this computer can encode is the table's pick; the person can choose another on the device's page). A mode is WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ; a codec's default mode is its largest at 30 frames a second. Audio: the page's audio list (FLAC up to 96 kHz and 24 bit, HE-AAC, LC-AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, WAV) is read as the receiver's for every device. Containers on the page: MP2T, MP3, MP4, OGG, WAV, WebM; Matroska is not named there (it is the review's first container for H.264, row 81). The order: AV1, HEVC, H.264, then VP9 and VP8: KPipeWire 6.7.4's libvpx encoders keep libvpx's default lag of 25 frames, so on a still screen (KWin sends a frame only when the screen changes) they give no picture; upstream KPipeWire sets lag-in-frames 0 since, and VP9 comes back before H.264 when our KPipeWire carries it.
